label: NETGEAR GS305EPP
description: 5-port gigabit smart switch with 4 PoE+ ports sharing a 120 W budget; port 5 is the unpowered uplink.
notes: Vendor figures from the GS305EP/GS305EPP/GS308EP/GS308EPP data sheet and the GS305EPP user manual: **5 gigabit copper ports, of which ports 1-4 carry PoE+ (802.3at) at up to 30 W per port and port 5 is the unpowered uplink**. Total PoE budget **120 W** - 4 x 30 W, so every powered port can be filled at its class ceiling. The GS305EP is the same 5-port body with a 63 W budget; the budget here is the P's.

poe.note: GS305EPP user manual, Hardware: "The switches provide 5 Gigabit Ethernet copper ports with 4 ports supporting up to 30W PoE+ (802.3at) per port"; "Model GS305EPP: The maximum PoE power budget of the switch across all active ports is 120W." The LED section is explicit about which socket is left out: "On models GS305EP and GS305EPP, ports 1 through 4 are PoE+ ports. Port 5 is an Ethernet (uplink) port." The data sheet's PoE table agrees - 4 PoE ports, 4 PoE+ 802.3at ports, Total PoE/PoE+ Budget 120W for GS305EPP (63W belongs to the GS305EP).
